note: Live on NEAR testnet since 2026-11-12. Contracts built from the stack head with rustc 1.86.0, cargo-near 0.22.0 and binaryen version_108 (market and mock_ft from contracts/artifacts). The keys stay on the operator box.
keepalive: Testnet contracts are left in place. Testnet NEAR has no value and the guest float is capped by the funding amount and the per-IP rate, not by reaping.

play.role: Guest funder and parent of every guest account. Holds a key separate from the root, so a leaked funder key can only spend the funder float.
play.note: Created with `near account create-account fund-myself play.nearcarta.testnet '… NEAR' autogenerate-new-keypair save-to-legacy-keychain sign-as nearcarta.testnet network-config testnet sign-with-legacy-keychain send`. Docs: https://docs.near.org/tools/cli

relayer.role: NEP-366 relayer float for the guest market moves.

board.wasm: built from contracts/charter_board at the stack head (network_of)
board.note: Built with the pinned toolchain in contracts/scripts/rebuild.sh (cargo-near 0.22.0). The board signs "testnet" into every propose_call_as message because its own account id ends in .testnet (contracts/charter_board/src/lib.rs `network_of`).

market.caps_note: city_payout_per_day is 2 NEAR, not the mainnet 0.08, because every guest sells to the same keeper shops: at 0.08 the city float would run out after about 40 guests. set_caps is owner-only and needs no redeploy.

house.wasm: built from contracts/house_nft at the stack head (new_with_board)
house.init_note: The mainnet init `new({owner})` keeps its hardcoded board and is not touched. The testnet record names the board through `new_with_board`, so no name is hardcoded for a network.

tusdc.note: NEP-141 test dollars for the welcome crate and the Payouts step. `mint` is open, so the funder can fill a guest's balance in one call.

toll.wasm: built from contracts/toll at the stack head
toll.init: new({owner, mpc, path, chain_id, foreign_address, fx_root_key, allow_to, max_per_tx, budget, max_fee_cap, verify_chain, token, dao, gate}) then set_price({board, fee, cost, splits, paused, usdc, max_token, hold_ns})
toll.note: The three empty fields are filled from `v1.signer-prod.testnet` `derived_public_key` with path base-1 and predecessor toll.nearcarta.testnet, read with a view call before the deploy. chain_id 84532 is Base Sepolia; contracts/toll/src/lib.rs `new` accepts 8453 or 84532.
toll.broadcast_note: `toll.cross` and `toll.sign_cross` run a real Chain Signatures request against v1.signer-prod.testnet and store the signature on chain. The backend does not send it to Base Sepolia: there is no funded Base Sepolia key, and the UI says the transaction is signed and not broadcast. Everything on the NEAR side is real and linked on testnet nearblocks.

base.name: Base Sepolia
base.note: No Base Sepolia ETH is held, so a crossing in the guest story is signed by the MPC network and NOT broadcast. The signed EIP-1559 transaction is shown with its hash and the exact basescan URL it would appear at. Docs: https://docs.base.org/base-chain/quickstart/connecting-to-base

keepers.note: Seeded by scripts/keepers-deploy.js with NEAR_NETWORK=testnet (steps keys, accounts, rows, market). Each keeper has a board row and a market shop.

planned.note: The shops a guest row may be opened against. shared/setup/open-row.js builds the receiver list from this file, so no account name is hardcoded in the guest defaults.

guest.note: The account name is base32(sha256(public_key))[0..10] plus the parent, so a retry is idempotent. The secret key never leaves the browser.

row.note: The guest defaults for /setup. 0.005 per action, 0.02 a day, 8 actions. 0.015 is spendable in the row: the order (0.001), the toll fee (0.001), the honest payment (0.0001) and the storage of each held call come out of it.

intents_note: NEAR Intents has no testnet deployment, so every Intents call from the guest story is a live dry quote against mainnet prices and says so in the UI.

shops.note: The shop names a guest row may reach. shared/net/net.js publishes this map on the page, so no page hardcodes an account id. `lookalike` is a typo-squat of the guard keeper that is on no row's receiver list: the board refuses a payment to it on chain (receiver_not_allowlisted) before any NEAR moves.
